identity.title: Non-Euclidean Gradient Descent Operates at the Edge of Stability

problem.claim: Explain the Edge of Stability phenomenon for gradient methods beyond the standard Euclidean setting.

gap.claim: Theoretical foundations for the widely observed EoS behavior remain incomplete despite its apparent conflict with classical smoothness assumptions.

contributions.claim: Interprets EoS through Directional Smoothness and extends this interpretation to arbitrary non-Euclidean norms.
Defines generalized sharpness under an arbitrary norm, covering vanilla and preconditioned GD as special cases and including several less-studied methods.
Provides a geometry-aware spectral diagnostic applicable across a broad class of non-Euclidean gradient methods.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their generalized sharpness framework by unifying Euclidean, preconditioned, and multiple non-Euclidean gradient methods under one arbitrary-norm formulation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that neural-network experiments show progressive sharpening followed by oscillations around or above the threshold 2/η for non-Euclidean GD using their generalized sharpness.

narrative_sequence.summary: Defines EoS as Hessian sharpness approaching and hovering near the stability threshold 2/η during GD.
Notes that EoS is widely observed in deep learning while its theoretical basis remains incomplete.
Interprets EoS via Directional Smoothness and generalizes sharpness to arbitrary norms.
Shows that the framework covers several gradient methods and reports analogous sharpening and oscillations in neural-network experiments.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a unifying arbitrary-norm definition with explicit special cases and a diagnostic application across methods.

lessons.interpretation: A framework claim becomes more transferable when its abstraction is tied to recognizable existing cases and an operational use.
lessons.application: When proposing a generalized optimization concept, state its reduction to established methods and identify a concrete diagnostic or analysis workflow it enables.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the proposed abstraction has no meaningful special cases or practical use described by the work.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the neural-network architectures, datasets, optimization settings, or quantitative experiment results.
It does not state formal theorems, guarantees, or proof details establishing the interpretation.
The scope of “broad class” and the behavior of each named method are not individually detailed.
